title: Search settings that repeat

blocks.text: A laundry's dispatch report is checked by two people every morning, and they must get the same routes from the same data. The routing code is fine; the search settings are not. Write `search_parameters(strategy, metaheuristic=None, solutions=None)` in `search.py`. It turns names such as `"SAVINGS"` and `"GUIDED_LOCAL_SEARCH"` into OR-Tools search parameters, and enforces the team's rule for repeatable runs:

items: the run never stops on wall time, so the parameters carry **no time limit**;
a metaheuristic that leaves local minima on purpose (anything but `GREEDY_DESCENT`) **always has a solution limit**: `solutions` if given, otherwise `DEFAULT_SOLUTIONS` (200);
`GREEDY_DESCENT` and the default search stop at their local minimum by themselves, so they get a solution limit only when `solutions` is given.

blocks.text: There is no model to formulate here: the routing model is fixed, and the choice is how to search it. Before you code, write the rule above as a small decision table (metaheuristic named or not, `solutions` given or not, the resulting `solution_limit`), and say which enum class each name belongs to in `routing_enums_pb2`.
The tests read the parameters and run one small model twice. About eight lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.constraint_solver import pywrapcp, routing_enums_pb2

DEFAULT_SOLUTIONS = 200


def search_parameters(strategy: str, metaheuristic: str | None = None, solutions: int | None = None):
    """Search parameters from names, for runs that repeat: a metaheuristic that escapes local
    minima always gets a solution limit (DEFAULT_SOLUTIONS when none is given), and no run gets
    a time limit."""
    params = pywrapcp.DefaultRoutingSearchParameters()
    params.first_solution_strategy = getattr(routing_enums_pb2.FirstSolutionStrategy, strategy)
    if metaheuristic is not None:
        params.local_search_metaheuristic = getattr(routing_enums_pb2.LocalSearchMetaheuristic, metaheuristic)
    if solutions is not None:
        params.solution_limit = solutions
    elif metaheuristic not in (None, "GREEDY_DESCENT"):
        params.solution_limit = DEFAULT_SOLUTIONS
    return params


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(search_parameters("SAVINGS", "GUIDED_LOCAL_SEARCH"))

cases.says: the strategy, metaheuristic and solution count named in the call are the ones the parameters hold
two runs with a fixed strategy, guided local search and a solution limit give the same routes and cost
a metaheuristic named without a solution count still gets one, the default of 200
no parameters carry a time limit, so no printed result depends on the machine's speed
greedy descent with no count named keeps the unlimited default, since it stops at its local minimum by itself

origin.section: Stop on Solutions, Not Seconds, When a Result Must Repeat

concepts: a first-solution strategy builds one complete set of routes, and some strategies build none on a given model
greedy descent stops at a local minimum, and a metaheuristic such as guided local search leaves it on purpose
a fixed strategy with a solution limit repeats, while a time limit depends on the machine
